**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). **4-bets frequently — not just vs me, also vs other players.** 3-bets extremely wide. **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything. C-bets most flops, BUT may check dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); REAL HANDS → continues aggressively (shoves with overpairs). Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **Facing donk-leads: calls one street then folds to continued pressure — CONFIRMED multiple times.** Fires big when opponent shows weakness — but if P2 checks after opponent shows weakness, P2 likely has air. **As 3-BET CALLER (OOP)**: More fit-or-fold than as PFA — folds to c-bets on boards where P2 whiffs. Folds to check-raise all-ins even in 3-bet pots. **Folds to flop raises in 4-bet pots** — c-bets then gives up when raised. **Consistently bleeding chips across sessions — confirmed exploitable.** **Exploit**: Flat P2's opens with suited broadways/connectors IP. Reserve 3-bets for QQ+/AKs (5-bet) and AQs/JJ (call 4-bet). When P2 calls 3-bet, c-bet most flops. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. Two-barrel bluffs effective. Raise turn bets as bluff.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled — most dangerous opponent. PERSISTENT LOSER across many sessions — likely overadjusting or running bad.** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium (suited aces, medium pairs). **3-bets from blinds vs ALL position opens** — blind 3-bet range is wider than typical. Calls 3-bets with medium pairs (99). **Confirmed trapper with WIDE check-raise range** — check-raises overpairs on wet boards for protection. River checks can still be traps. **Folds dry/disconnected boards without connections. Triple-barrels with one-pair value hands.** Floating P3 is LOW EV — only continue with strong draws (9+ outs) or made hands. **On wet boards in 3-bet pots, P3 checks strong hands to set up check-raises.** **Exploit**: C-bet when P3 checks disconnected/dry boards. Don't value-bet thin on river. Call P3's 3-bets IP with strong suited hands — P3 gives up without connection. On wet boards, be prepared to call check-raises with overpairs.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~50%), passive preflop, MIXED postflop. CONSISTENT CHIP ACCUMULATOR — frequently ends as table chip leader.** Calls 3-bets with suited junk. Limp-reraise = strong. Shoves AA. EXTREMELY sticky — calls river with bottom pair, 9-high, calls massive overbets. Check-raises turn with made hands. **Also EXTREMELY PASSIVE with strong hands** — checks made straights through ALL streets on scary boards. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+). Does NOT always fold to 4-bets — calls with QQ+/AK likely and plays very aggressively postflop.** When P4 calls a 4-bet, their range is NUTTED. As single-raiser PFA: C-bets flop then gives up on turn — FLOATABLE. Do NOT float vs P4's 3-bets. **Exploit**: 3-bet for VALUE only. Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target). NEVER bluff. Check strong hands to induce — but also bet for value since P4 checks strong hands passively. Respect check-raises/donk-bets/limp-reraises/3-bets. If P4 calls a 4-bet, proceed with extreme caution.

**Player 5**: **Tight (~10-15% VPIP), but STICKIER than typical nit with pocket pairs.** Opens hands like A8s in position. Cold-calls 3-bets with medium pairs. **Will call down with underpairs** — called all-in with 99 on T-high board. **As PFA**: C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. Single donk-bet → folds to raises/turn barrels. **Call flop → raise turn = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Call flop c-bets wider — P5 gives up on turn. Do NOT multi-barrel bluff when P5 shows pair commitment.

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wider than initially estimated.** Limps with total trash. Opens wide. **Makes MASSIVE overbets for value** — will overbet 30x+ pot with made hands on river. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED (AA confirmed), non-shove 4-bets may be slightly wider.** As PFA: C-bets flop then folds to turn donk-leads. Folds big pairs on ace-high boards. **Exploit**: Value bet extremely wide postflop — P6 pays off. Bluff ace-high boards as PFA. Isolate limps with wide value range. Fold to 4-bet shoves. Respect massive overbets (P6 has it).

**Player 7**: **Wide opener, passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop.** Folds to 3-bets after cold-calling opens. **CAN 3-bet but very rare — and folds to 4-bets.** P7's 3-bet range is strong-but-not-premium (JJ/TT/AQ type). Donk-leads and triple-barrels with strength. Raises flop with top pair on paired boards. Sticky as caller. **Exploit**: Value bet relentlessly and size up. Don't bluff once they've shown aggression. 3-bet to isolate when P7 cold-calls. 4-bet P7's rare 3-bets — P7 folds.

## My Table Image & Approach

**Image: VERY TIGHT.** After latest session (~10% VPIP, card-dead), image is even tighter than usual. This means MAXIMUM fold equity entering next session — exploit early with wider steals before image loosens. VPIP across 12+ sessions averages 20-25% but fluctuates with cards dealt.

## Core Strategy

1. **VPIP target: 20-25%.** Tight image = fold equity = primary profit. Proven over 12+ sessions (240+ hands).
2. **SUITED is king**: Suited broadways and suited connectors are highest-EV aggression hands. Offsuit broadways only AJo+ from CO/BTN. K-x suited, A-x suited profitable steals.
3. **Station exploit (P2, P4, P5 w/pairs, P6, P7)**: Value bet wide, NEVER bluff postflop, isolate limps.
4. **P2 preflop**: Flat P2's opens with suited broadways/connectors IP. Reserve 3-bets for QQ+/AKs (5-bet) and AQs/JJ (call 4-bet). When P2 calls 3-bet, c-bet most boards.
5. **P4**: ONLY float vs single raise. RESPECT 3-bets AND 4-bet calls. Value bet wide — P4 is #1 target. Don't wait for P4 to bet — P4 checks made hands through all streets.
6. **P5**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Call flop c-bets wider. Do NOT multi-barrel when P5 shows pair commitment.
7. **P6**: Isolate limps wide for value. FOLD to 4-bet shoves. Value bet wide postflop. Respect massive overbets.
8. **P3 (skilled)**: Call 3-bets IP with strong suited hands. Avoid thin river value. DO NOT float without 9+ clean outs. Expect wet-board check-raises.
9. **P7**: 4-bet their rare 3-bets — P7 folds. Value bet relentlessly.
10. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P4 (accumulator) > P7 (aggressive) > P2 (LAG volume) > P5 (sticky pairs) > P6 (spewy).
11. **SMALL/MEDIUM PAIRS (22-88)**: Set-mine cheaply only. Check-fold on miss.
12. **Win mechanism**: Profits from preflop/flop aggression with fold equity + value betting stations. Both engines essential.
